Conflict: Material Design recommends a recycled PC/ABS blend for circularity, while In-Service rejects this due to lower impact resistance and instead recommends a high-impact polycarbonate shell with mechanically fastened grips to ensure durability.
Decision: Monolithic high-impact polycarbonate (PC) shell with mechanically fastened elastomer grips
Rationale: Applying the priority hierarchy, regulatory compliance with ESPR Annex I (a) regarding product durability and reliability is critical to prevent premature failure. While recycled PC/ABS supports recycled content goals, a failure in drop durability would lead to premature disposal. Mechanically fastened grips satisfy both the In-Service requirement for durability and the Circularity requirement to avoid overmolded materials that contaminate the recycling stream.

Conflict: Circularity and In-Service recommend standardized threaded fasteners to allow non-destructive disassembly, whereas Manufacturing highlights that this increases assembly complexity and part count compared to automated ultrasonic welding or adhesive bonding.
Decision: Threaded metal inserts with standardized Torx screws
Rationale: Regulatory compliance with ESPR Annex I (b) and (c) mandates ease of non-destructive disassembly and repair. Although adhesive bonding or ultrasonic welding optimizes manufacturing efficiency and reduces initial assembly costs, these permanent joining methods prevent repair and clean material separation at end-of-life, directly violating non-negotiable circularity requirements.

Conflict: In-Service and Circularity recommend a brushless DC motor with a modular gearbox to maximize technical lifetime and repairability, whereas Manufacture rejects this due to the high energy consumption and hazardous waste generated during the production of brushless electronic controllers.
Decision: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with modular planetary gearbox and separable neodymium magnets
Rationale: Under the ESPR lifecycle perspective, the extended technical lifetime, reliability, and in-use energy efficiency of a brushless motor (Annex I (a) and (g)) outweigh the higher manufacturing-stage environmental footprint. Designing the motor with separable magnets also addresses critical raw material recovery requirements under Annex I (d).

Conflict: Circularity recommends passive cooling with open ventilation slots to avoid complex active components, while In-Service rejects this because open vents allow dust and debris ingress that degrades internal electronics and reduces tool reliability.
Decision: Closed-loop heat pipe with external aluminum heatsink fins
Rationale: Ensuring the tool's durability and reliability (Annex I (a)) in harsh operating environments is a primary regulatory objective. A closed-loop system prevents internal contamination and premature failure, while the external aluminum heatsink avoids the use of thermal potting compounds, which Circularity notes are highly detrimental to end-of-life recycling (Annex I (e)).

Conflict: Circularity and In-Service recommend a highly modular, plug-connected architecture to facilitate easy repair and component replacement, whereas Manufacture recommends a monolithic integrated design to optimize automated high-volume assembly and minimize production waste.
Decision: Modular architecture with separate, plug-connected sub-assemblies (cartridge-based)
Rationale: ESPR Annex I (b) and (c) explicitly prioritize ease of repair, maintenance, and modularity. A monolithic integrated design, while highly efficient for manufacturing, creates a high risk of premature obsolescence since the failure of a single sub-component (like a switch) would force the disposal of the entire tool.

Conflict: Material Design and Circularity recommend a removable, slide-on lithium-ion battery pack to ensure repairability and battery recycling, whereas Manufacture recommends a corded AC power supply to completely avoid the high energy consumption and hazardous waste associated with battery cell production.
Decision: Removable, slide-on Li-ion battery pack with standardized interface and screw-fastened casing
Rationale: A corded power supply directly undermines the core functional performance and conditions of use (Annex I (s)) of a cordless screwdriver. To balance this with circularity, a removable, slide-on battery pack with a standardized interface ensures the battery can be replaced as a consumable (Annex I (l)) and easily disassembled for recycling.
